files.purpose: Single shared macOS Keychain implementation (generic-password SecItem calls) for every native provider API key, replacing four identical per-provider copies; one Keychain service (AppInfo.name) with one item per provider account name.
key_symbols: static func key(for account: String, fallback: String) -> String
@discardableResult static func setKey(_ key: String, account: String) -> Bool
private static func read(_ account: String) -> String?
private static func delete(_ account: String)
state_owned: No stored state of its own; all state lives in the macOS Keychain under service AppInfo.name keyed by account string
side_effects: Keychain writes via SecItemAdd
Keychain deletes via SecItemDelete (always called before an add, so setKey replaces rather than duplicates)
Keychain reads via SecItemCopyMatching
platform_assumptions: kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlocked accessibility level (key readable only while the Mac is unlocked)
persisted_fields: Keychain generic password item: kSecAttrService = AppInfo.name, kSecAttrAccount = provider account string, kSecValueData = UTF-8 trimmed key, kSecAttrAccessible = kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlocked
feature_notes: key(for:fallback:) returns "" (empty string) when CaptureRun.isEnabled, so a capture/replay run never touches real credentials
Read value is trimmed of whitespace and newlines; an empty/whitespace-only stored value is treated as absent and the fallback is used
setKey trims the input; an empty trimmed key deletes the item and returns true
setKey returns the Bool result of SecItemAdd(...) == errSecSuccess so the caller knows whether a UserDefaults fallback copy is still needed
read uses kSecReturnData true with kSecMatchLimitOne
unresolved_questions: AppInfo.name is defined outside this bundle, so the literal Keychain service string is not established here
CaptureRun is defined outside this bundle; only its isEnabled gate is visible

files.purpose: Sandboxed file primitives (path resolution inside the project root, read with line slicing and size caps, atomic write, single-occurrence edit, recursive and flat listing) used by the native OpenAI-compatible agent tool loop.

func resolveURL(_ path: String) throws -> URL
state_owned: static Mutations actor serializing all write and edit operations process-wide across every NativeFileTools instance
side_effects: File reads through FileHandle
Directory creation with createDirectory(withIntermediateDirectories: true)
Atomic file writes (Data.write(options: .atomic) and String.write(atomically: true))
Directory enumeration
platform_assumptions: POSIX path semantics: "/" prefix for absolute, "~" expansion via NSString.expandingTildeInPath, containment checked as root.path + "/" prefix
FileManager enumerator options .skipsHiddenFiles and .skipsPackageDescendants (macOS bundle packages)
feature_notes: readLimit = 1_000_000 bytes; the read loop pulls chunks of min(65_536, readLimit + 1 - data.count) so it can detect an over-limit file
Oversize file error: "That file is too large to read (<byteCount> bytes)." with the byte count from handle.seekToEnd()
Text decoding tries UTF-8 first then .isoLatin1; failing both gives "That file is not readable as text."
Path escape error: "That path is outside the project. Stay inside <workingDirectory>."
Empty path error: "A file path is required."
Missing file error: "No such file: <displayPath>."; missing directory error: "No such directory: <displayPath>."

With startLine or lineCount, output is prefixed "(lines <first>-<last> of <count>)\n"; default lineCount is 200, startLine is clamped to at least 1, and a start past the end returns "(the file has <n> lines; start_line <first> is past the end)"

Whole-file reads over 60_000 characters are truncated to the first 60_000 with "\n…(truncated, <n> chars total; read the rest with start_line and line_count)"; the utf8 byte count is checked first as a cheap bound

editFile requires exactly one occurrence: zero gives "That exact text was not found in <path>. Read the file and copy it exactly.", more than one gives "That text appears <n> times in <path>. Include more context so it matches once."; an empty old_string gives "old_string must not be empty. Read the file first, then edit an exact block."
writeFile encoding failure: "Could not encode that content."
skippedDirectories = [".git", "node_modules", ".build", "build", "dist", "DerivedData", "Pods", "target", ".venv", "venv"]
listFiles caps at 300 entries and appends "…(truncated)" as entry 301 (reserveCapacity(301)); empty results return "(empty)"

Non-recursive listing sorts entries, skips .DS_Store by prefix, and appends "/" to directory names; recursive listing skips directories themselves and emits file paths relative to the working directory
Every long-running loop calls try Task.checkCancellation() so a stopped turn aborts mid-read or mid-edit
unresolved_questions: ToolTitles.relativePath behavior for a path outside the root is defined elsewhere
The Mutations actor is static, so writes serialize across all sessions and projects; whether that cross-project serialization is intended is not stated in the file

File reads, writes and edits through NativeFileTools

/usr/bin/grep at a fixed absolute path for search_text

Approval prompts: "Read <path>", "Search for “<pattern>”", "Write <path>", "Edit <path>", "Call <server> <name>", and the raw command text for run_command

Tool row titles: read_file uses the display path; list_files uses the working directory last path component when the path is empty; search_text uses the pattern or "Search"; run_command uses the command or "Run command"; unknown tools use the tool name
Decline output: tool row shows "The user declined this action." and the model receives "The user declined this action. Ask how to proceed instead of retrying it."
Notice: "<title> paused after 200 rounds of tool calls in one turn. Say “continue” to pick up where it left off."
Notice: "<title> lost the connection while answering. That reply was cut off, and this response is restarting."
Notice: "Nothing to compact yet." and "Context compacted."
Error: "<title> rejected the API key. Check it in Settings → Providers → <title>."
Error: "<title> could not reach the network after 3 attempts. Check the connection, then try again." optionally followed by " (<transport reason>)"
Write result text "Wrote <path> (<n> bytes)."; edit result text "Edited <path>."; command result "(exit <code>, no output)" or "exit <code>\n<output>"
MCP empty error output "Error: the MCP tool reported failure with no output."; empty success output shown as "(no output)"
Unknown tool: row output "Unknown tool." and model result "Error: unknown tool <name>."
Stopped tool output: "Stopped."
feature_notes: maxRoundsPerTurn = 200, a runaway guard only; hitting it emits the pause notice and reports status .interrupted, keeping history so "continue" resumes

condenseHistoryAt = 160_000, condenseHistoryTo = 100_000, condenseKeepsRecent = 10, condensedMarker = "…[Droppy Code condensed this output"; a condensed tool result keeps its first 400 characters and appends "\n…[Droppy Code condensed this output (<n> bytes); call the tool again if you need it]", and only results over 1_200 bytes are condensed
maxTransportRetries = 2 with transportRetryDelays [.seconds(1), .seconds(2)]; only URLError .networkConnectionLost, .timedOut and .cannotConnectToHost are retried

A response that already streamed a Hydra head delegation (HydraPrompts.streamedDelegations(in: content)) is never retried; the error text appends "This response was not retried because it had already streamed a head delegation."
StreamCoalescer batches consecutive text or reasoning and flushes at most 30 ms (.milliseconds(30)) after the first piece; switching between text and reasoning forces an immediate flush
SSE drain: lines are trimmed, only lines with the "data:" prefix are used, "[DONE]" ends the stream, and json["error"] yields a stream error using error.message or displayText

Usage parsing accepts prompt_tokens or input_tokens, completion_tokens or output_tokens, prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens or input_tokens_details.cached_tokens or prompt_cache_hit_tokens, and total_tokens falling back to input + output
Delta parsing reads choices[0].delta.content, delta.reasoning_content or delta.reasoning, and delta.tool_calls[].index/.id/.function.name/.function.arguments with index defaulting to 0
Non-200 responses read up to 8_000 characters of the body; errorMessage prefers error.message then message, else the first 500 characters of the trimmed body, else "<title> returned status <code>."
Six built-in tools with the exact names read_file, list_files, search_text, write_file, edit_file, run_command, plus MCP tools appended; tool_choice is "auto" and stream is true

read_file description states the whole file by default and start_line/line_count for large files; edit_file requires old_string to appear exactly once and also accepts legacy argument names old_text and new_text

readOnlyKind maps read_file to .read and list_files/search_text to .search; consecutive approval-free reads run concurrently with maxConcurrentReads = 4 while preserving the model order, and anything else acts as a barrier
requiresApproval: plan mode blocks .edit and .command even after "Approve for turn"; supervised asks for everything; autoAcceptEdits and auto ask only for .command; fullAccess asks for nothing
trimHistory keeps the system message plus at most 50 body messages once the count exceeds 60, and never cuts the running turn because it slices from the last user message
compact() keeps the system message plus the last 10 messages, only when messages.count > 12, then sanitizes
sanitizeHistory drops orphaned tool messages and strips tool_calls that lost their answers, deleting an assistant message that ends up with neither calls nor content
Output summary limits per tool: read_file 4_000, list_files 4_000, search_text 6_000, MCP 12_000, run_command 12_000 characters, each with "\n…(truncated)"

searchText runs /usr/bin/grep with ["-R", "-n", "-I", "--exclude-dir=.git", "--exclude-dir=node_modules", "--exclude-dir=.build", "--exclude-dir=build"], then -E or -F, then "--", pattern, target; timeout 30, outputLimit 64_000; results cap at 120 lines with "\n…(<n> matches, truncated)" and "(no matches)" when empty; the path goes through NativeFileTools.resolveURL so it cannot escape the project, fixing a noted past vulnerability that grepped ~/.ssh
runCommand runs /bin/zsh -lc with LoginEnvironment.current, timeout 120, outputLimit 24_000, and prefixes an over-24_000-byte output with "…" keeping the suffix

System prompt opens "You are Droppy Code’s <agentIdentity(model)>, working inside <workingDirectory> on macOS." with four mode-line variants (plan, build+supervised, build+autoAcceptEdits/auto, build+fullAccess), then six Rules bullets including "Never hard-wrap prose at a fixed column" and "Today’s date is <ISO8601 now>", then the Hydra policy, the AntiSlopPolicy instructions and the project guidance block
refreshSystemPrompt rewrites messages[0] at the start of each turn so edited AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md rules take effect on a resumed thread

Images: at most 4 attachments where isImage, only when config.isVisionModel(currentModel); otherwise the text gains "\n\n[Attached images (model cannot see them): <names>]"; images are sent as {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:<mime>;base64,<data>"}}
assistantTurn always sets role and content, adds reasoning_content only when config.replaysReasoning, and adds tool_calls entries of {id, type: "function", function: {name, arguments}}

start() reuses configuration.resumeID or a lowercased UUID, seeds the messages array with the system prompt plus the saved transcript mapped to user/assistant roles, and deliberately emits no .models event because the registry owns the live catalog

Hydra head pacing: budgetSpent when toolsUsed >= HydraBudget.maxTools or elapsed >= HydraBudget.maxSeconds, a one-time wrap-up note at wrapUpTools or wrapUpSeconds, and a pacing note every HydraBudget.pacingTools tools without a write_file or edit_file
The final-report round (input.isFinalReport or budget spent) is streamed with withTools: false
reportUsage emits .usage plus TokenLedger.shared.record(spend:) and a .tokenSpend event only when ReportedTokenUsage.hasSpend (total, input or output greater than zero)
nextID format is "<prefix>-<counter>-<first 8 characters of a UUID>" with prefixes "message", "thought", "tool", "approval", "plan"
In plan mode a non-empty final text emits .planCompleted(id: "plan-...", markdown: finalText) before .turnCompleted
answerQuestion(_:answers:) is an empty no-op: these providers never ask structured questions

The base applyProviderPayload and reasoningEffort(for:model:) pair is effectively dead in shipped code: all three subclasses override applyProviderPayload without calling super, and reasoningEffort(for:model:) always returns nil
unresolved_questions: Config.maxOutputTokens is stored but never read inside this file; Z.ai sends max_tokens itself in its override, so the field appears unused by the base class
statusCode inside performStream is a let bound to 200 and never updated on the streaming path, so a mid-stream error reaches friendlyError with statusCode 200
HydraBudget constant values (pacingTools, maxTools, maxSeconds, wrapUpTools, wrapUpSeconds) and the exact note texts are defined outside this bundle

If the cleaned reply fails the usable() filter, the first non-empty line of the raw reply is trimmed the same way and retried
usable() rejects: empty, longer than 64 characters, more than 9 whitespace-separated words, containing a newline or "?", ending in one of ":;,!…"

usable() rejects openers ["i ", "i'", "sorry", "sure", "here", "please", "could you", "can you", "what ", "it seems", "it looks", "unfortunately", "there is no", "not enough", "need more", "maybe ", "the request", "this request"]
usable() rejects phrases ["more context", "meaningful title", "as an ai", "cannot", "can't", "unable to"]

Commit prompt rules: an imperative subject line of at most 72 characters with no trailing period, optionally a blank line plus a few short bullets, reply with the message only without code fences; summary truncated to 6_000 characters and patch to 40_000
Commit output strips every "```" occurrence and trims whitespace; an empty result becomes nil

Claude engine flags: ["-p", "--output-format", "text", "--model", "haiku", "--tools", "", "--disable-slash-commands", "--strict-mcp-config", "--permission-mode", "dontAsk", "--no-session-persistence"] with timeout 120 and the prompt on stdin, reading result.trimmedOutput

Codex engine flags: ["exec", "--ephemeral", "--skip-git-repo-check", "-s", "read-only", "--model", <model>, "--config", "model_reasoning_effort=\"low\"", "--output-last-message", <temp path>, "-"] with timeout 180; the answer is read back from the output file rather than stdout
Both engines return nil when the process fails (result.succeeded false) or produces empty output
The usable() doc comment cites a real failure: "I need more context to create a meaningful title. What spec…" once reached a chat name

Model entry "GLM-5.3 Flash" detail "Fast, reads images · 1M context" (id glm-5.3-flash, defaultEffort "max")
Window titles "5-hour limit" and "Weekly" when the unit cannot be derived, and "Monthly · MCP tools" for TIME_LIMIT entries
Window detail strings "<current> of <usage> credits" and "<current> of <usage> calls" with thousands separators

zaiEfforts = ["low", "high", "max"]; contextWindow = 1_000_000; maxOutputTokens = 128_000

option(for:) offers only glm-5.3 and glm-5.3-flash by name; unknown ids are accepted only when they have the "glm-5.3" prefix and do not contain "flashx", because GLM-5.3-FlashX is on the account list but refused by the plan with business code 1311 before any credit is spent
isVisionModel returns false for a nil id, otherwise true when the id contains "flash" or ends with "v"
planLimits requires HTTP 200 and then json["code"] == 200 or json["success"] == true, then fills PlanLimits.resetCredits from resetCredits()
limits(from:) reads data.level through PlanLimitsReader.planName and labels the plan "Coding Plan <name>"; entries come from data.limits
Per entry it reads type, usage, currentValue, percentage (or current/usage*100), clamped to 0...100, and nextResetTime in milliseconds divided by 1_000 for a Date
Unit codes map to minutes: 3 gives number * 60 (hours), 4 gives number * 1_440 (days), 6 gives number * 10_080 (weeks), 5 gives number * 43_200 (months); anything else leaves minutes nil
CREDIT_LIMIT and TOKENS_LIMIT entries become windows with id "credit-<n>"; TIME_LIMIT entries become id "tools-<n>"; other types are skipped, and an empty window list returns nil

resetCredits iterates [("fiveHourResets", "FIVE_HOUR", "Resets the 5-hour limit"), ("weekResets", "WEEK", "Resets the weekly limit")], skipping cards where available is explicitly false or recordId is missing, and builds ids of the form "<TYPE>:<recordId>"

consumeResetCredit splits the id on the first ":", POSTs {"targetType": "PERSONAL", "resetType": <type>, "recordId": <int>, "requestId": <lowercased UUID>} with timeoutInterval 20, requires code 200 and success true, sleeps 2 seconds, and returns .reset
Card expiry strings are parsed as naive "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss" in Asia/Shanghai
formatCount uses a decimal NumberFormatter pinned to Locale("en_US") with maximumFractionDigits 0, falling back to "\(Int(value))"
unresolved_questions: PlanLimitsReader.planName and windowTitle(minutes:), and the PlanLimits and ResetCreditError declarations, are outside this bundle
Unit code 5 is mapped to 43_200 minutes (30 days) as a month, but the API meaning of each unit code is not documented in the file

applyProviderPayload sets tool_stream = true only when withTools, always sets thinking = {"type": "enabled", "clear_thinking": false} so prior thinking is kept, and max_tokens = 128_000 (ZaiAPI.maxOutputTokens)
reasoningEffort maps "low" to "low", "medium" and "high" to "high", "xhigh"/"extra-high"/"max" to "max", and anything else to nil

friendlyError branch order is deliberate and documented: the context-length branch runs first because a context message also contains the word "limit", and the plan-window branch ("usage limit"/"limit exhausted"/"extra usage") is late so a throttle is never reported as a spent window

Business codes named in the comments: 1311 model not in plan, 1302 and 1305 rate limit and overload, 1313 Fair Usage Policy, 1113 no resource package, 1309 package expired, 1314 and 1315 enterprise, 1308/1310/1316-1321 spent window, 1211 unknown model
The literal string "usage limit" in the plan-window message is what auto-continue listens for before reading the reset time from the quota API
planRefusedModel extracts the text after a case-insensitive "access to " match, trimming whitespace, newlines and the characters ".`\"'", defaulting to "that model"
unresolved_questions: The auto-continue component that watches for "usage limit" lives outside this bundle, so the exact matching there is not verified here
